name: Fin + Dut protocol

lead: Fin + dut refers to taking the two prescription 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, finasteride and dutasteride, together in an attempt to block the conversion of testosterone to DHT, the hormone linked to follicle miniaturisation in male pattern hair loss. The appearance goal is keeping or regaining scalp hair density and hairline.

The pairing is discussed mainly on looksmax.org, often by users who also take testosterone or other androgens and are concerned about hair loss. Published literature describes each drug separately for hair loss and prostate disease; the combination is not an approved regimen and is not the subject of dedicated trials cited here.

paras: On forums, users describe adding one drug to the other, often alongside topical or oral minoxidil, and ask how to get DHT as low as possible. Both drugs require a prescription in most countries. Posts discuss differences in how long each drug stays in the body and whether to stagger them. This wiki does not give dosing or sourcing.

Both drugs carry documented adverse effects including sexual dysfunction, mood changes and, for pregnant partners and fetuses, birth-defect risk; reviews discuss a reported persistent syndrome after finasteride. They also lower PSA, which affects prostate screening. Forum users acknowledge side effects, and one reply to a guide thread jokes that readers do not care about them. A prescriber is the usual route for monitoring.

chain: Follicles are exposed to less of the hormone that drives miniaturisation
Hair density and hairline are better preserved
angle.text: Users aim to keep a fuller hairline and denser scalp hair by pushing DHT lower than a single drug does. It is most often discussed by people on testosterone or other androgens who expect faster balding.

lead: The fin + dut protocol is a looksmaxxing and hair-loss forum term for using finasteride and dutasteride together. Both are 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors: they reduce the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which shrinks scalp follicles in androgenetic alopecia.[1][2] Users adopt the pairing to suppress DHT more completely than either drug alone, to protect hair density and hairline, particularly while using testosterone or other androgens.[3][4]

Finasteride inhibits type II and III 5-alpha-reductase, while dutasteride inhibits types I, II and III and lowers blood DHT more deeply and stays in the body for weeks.[1][5] Dutasteride is approved for male hair loss in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan, and in the United States it is approved for prostate enlargement, with hair-loss use off-label.[1]

Reviews describe each drug's benefits and side effects individually; no controlled trial of the combination for hair loss is cited here, and the practice is documented chiefly through forum discussion.[2][5][6]
infobox: Prescription; combination is an informal forum practice

paras: The protocol combines finasteride, the older and better-known hair-loss pill, with dutasteride, which inhibits an additional enzyme isoform. Because 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to the more potent DHT, blocking it reduces DHT in scalp and blood.[1][2] One looksmax.org guide explains the pair in these terms and describes minoxidil as a separate, circulation- and follicle-activity-based treatment.[3]

In forum threads the pairing appears in several settings: users on testosterone who notice miniaturisation ask how to get DHT as low as possible,[4] users ask about nuclear options when they want hair loss treatment,[7] and others discuss telling a balding relative about fin and dut.[8]

Dutasteride inhibits all three 5-alpha-reductase isoforms and can lower blood DHT by up to about 98 percent versus roughly 65-70 percent for finasteride, according to Wikipedia; its elimination half-life is about 4-5 weeks against 5-8 hours for finasteride.[1] A review of dutasteride in androgenetic alopecia and an overview of 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors cover the chemistry and clinical data.[5][9]

Because finasteride's half-life is short and dutasteride's long, forum posters discuss whether and how to combine them.[4] Published clinical sources describe single-drug use, so these schedules rest on user experience.

No published trial of the finasteride plus dutasteride combination for hair loss is cited here. Studies and reviews cover each drug alone: dutasteride in androgenetic alopecia has been summarised in an update review,[5] and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors' safety has been reviewed systematically.[2] A comparative study looked at low-dose oral minoxidil with spironolactone versus finasteride or dutasteride in female pattern hair loss.[10]

A systematic review of finasteride and dutasteride safety notes that patients are expected to take them indefinitely despite limited research on long-term adverse effects, and that the NIH added a rare-disease listing for post-finasteride syndrome.[2] A meta-analysis of randomised trials in benign prostatic hyperplasia examined sexual side effects of 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors.[11] Wikipedia lists decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and breast enlargement among reported effects of dutasteride, and says it is contraindicated in pregnancy because of risk to male fetuses.[1] The drugs also lower PSA, which can complicate prostate screening.[1][12]

On looksmax.org, hair loss is treated as a major threat to appearance, and fin and dut are discussed as the strongest oral options, together with minoxidil.[3] One reply to the guide thread jokes that readers do not care about side effects, while the guide's author answers that some people do, and a separate thread title warns about alcohol use on the drugs.[3][13] Users who use TRT or other androgens often raise the pairing as insurance against balding.[4][14]

lore.intro: Fin + dut appears on looksmax.org as a high-intensity hair-retention approach, often in the context of testosterone use.[3][4][14]
